vocabulary.meaning_en: a situation where people have different opinions
vocabulary.example: There was a lot of disagreement in the meeting.
I understand your point of view.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an idea or opinion in a discussion
share many ideas quickly in a group
vocabulary.example: Let's brainstorm ideas for the launch.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the start of selling a new product
something a company makes to sell
vocabulary.example: Our latest product is the Imperial Lemon.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the set of colours used in a design
vocabulary.example: The colour scheme will be green and yellow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a lower price for a short time
vocabulary.example: We could make a special opening offer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money taken off the normal price
vocabulary.example: They offered 20% off: a big discount.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the chance that something bad may happen
vocabulary.example: That would be a big risk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: without money to pay what you owe
vocabulary.example: If we do that, we'll be bankrupt!

vocabulary.meaning_en: a client who buys from you often
vocabulary.example: We'll give the offer to all regular clients.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the last choice that ends a discussion
angry and ready to attack or argue
annoyed because you can't do what you want
vocabulary.example: I'm so frustrated! I can't find the words.
They're desperate to sell their lemons.

vocabulary.meaning_en: throw away or sell something you don't want
vocabulary.example: We need to get rid of these old boxes.

fine_lines.title: No, you're wrong vs I see your point, but...
fine_lines.explanation_ar: قول No, you're wrong أو I disagree مباشرة قد يبدو عدوانيًا. الأفضل أن تُظهر احترامك لرأي الآخر ثم تقول رأيك: I see your point, but actually I think...
fine_lines.explanation_en: "No, you're wrong" can sound aggressive. It is better to accept the other idea first, then give yours: I see your point, but actually I think...

examples.sentence: I see your point, but actually I think 10% is better. (polite)

fine_lines.title: disagree vs disagreement
fine_lines.explanation_ar: disagree فعل: I disagree with you. أما disagreement فاسم: There is a disagreement.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Disagree" is a verb; "disagreement" is a noun.

examples.sentence: We had a small disagreement about the price.

expressions.phrase: Well, I'm not so sure about that...
expressions.meaning_en: A soft way to disagree. Then give your reason.
expressions.example: Well, I'm not so sure about that. The price may be too high.

expressions.phrase: I see your point, but actually I think...
expressions.meaning_ar: أفهم وجهة نظرك، لكنني في الواقع أعتقد...
expressions.meaning_en: Accept the other idea, then politely give yours.
expressions.example: I see your point, but actually I think we should wait.

expressions.meaning_en: Start a sentence with "But" to disagree with what was just said.
expressions.example: But having three colours would work better.

expressions.meaning_en: Agree with part of someone's idea.
expressions.example: That's a good point. Let's think about it.

expressions.phrase: That would be a big risk.
expressions.meaning_en: Say an idea could be dangerous for the business.
expressions.example: Giving everyone 50% off would be a big risk.

expressions.phrase: Why don't we offer a special offer?
expressions.meaning_en: Suggest an idea in a meeting.
expressions.example: Why don't we offer new clients a special offer?

grammar.title: Polite disagreement: soften, then give a reason
grammar.explanation_ar: لتختلف بأدب: 1) ابدأ بعبارة لطيفة: Well, I'm not so sure about that / I see your point, but... 2) قل رأيك مع actually أو I think. 3) اذكر السبب. ولا تكن عدوانيًا.
grammar.explanation_en: To disagree politely: 1) start softly (Well, I'm not so sure about that / I see your point, but...), 2) give your idea with "actually" or "I think", 3) give a reason.
examples: Well, I'm not so sure about that. I think it will be too expensive.
I see your point, but actually I think the clients will like it.
But if we wait, we might lose the client.

grammar.title: First conditional for results
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم If + مضارع بسيط، ثم will + فعل لنتحدث عن نتيجة محتملة في المستقبل: If we do that, all our clients will ask for 20% off.
grammar.explanation_en: Use If + present simple, then will + verb, to talk about a likely future result.
examples: If we do that, we'll be bankrupt.
If the clients are happy, they will come back.
If we give a discount, we will sell more.

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to disagree?
choices: I see your point, but actually I think...
questions.explanation_ar: I see your point, but... هي الطريقة المهذبة.
questions.explanation_en: "I see your point, but..." is polite.

questions.question: Well, I'm not so sure ___ that.
questions.explanation_ar: العبارة: not so sure about that.
questions.explanation_en: The phrase is "not so sure about that".

questions.question: If we ___ 20% off, all clients will want it.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد if في الشرط الأول نستخدم المضارع البسيط.

questions.question: "Brainstorm" means...
choices: share many ideas in a group
questions.explanation_ar: brainstorm تعني تبادل الأفكار في مجموعة.
questions.explanation_en: It means share many ideas in a group.

questions.question: After you disagree, you should...
questions.explanation_en: Give a reason for your opinion.

questions.question: "That would be a big risk" means...
questions.explanation_en: A risk means something bad could happen.

questions.question: If we're not careful, we ___ bankrupt.
A word you can start a sentence with to disagree:
questions.explanation_ar: يمكن البدء بـ But للتعبير عن الاختلاف.
